analysis.title: Duttenhoefer's Daily 19.10.2026
key_insights: S&P 500 fell 109bps to 7659 (+12% ytd) to close a turbulent week. Nasdaq lost more than 5% on the week, the largest weekly loss since Liberation Day. SOX had an 8-day losing streak (longest since 2008) and US banks fell 6 straight weeks (also longest since 2008).
Mag-7 outperformed the Nasdaq on 10 of 11 sessions. US 10yr yield fell to 5.06%, VIX rose 21% to 20 (highest since July), Brent is $108, Gold $4181 (-3% ytd) and Bitcoin $83k (-6% ytd).

Middle East: Brent at $108 as Iran placed its forces on highest alert for 72 hours and mobile bomb shelters are being rapidly deployed in Tel Aviv. Putin proposed a summit with Trump and Xi on a Ukraine deal.

Friday showed the first real sign of panic in index protection: VIX futures traded 3.6x the 20-day average, VIX call volume was the 2nd-highest in 5 years, and Cboe index put volume was a record daily high.
Positioning: US L/S net leverage fell 3.2pts last week (4th-largest in 5 years). Global Tech saw its largest percentage net selling on record since 2016.

Goldman Sachs upgrades equities back to Overweight for 3 months (in line with 12 months), citing supportive earnings growth and a valuation de-rating that improves asymmetry into Q3 earnings. It also moves to Overweight bonds for 12 months, as long-duration bonds offer better medium-term value with inflation normalising and central bank pricing less hawkish.
SOXL (3x levered semi bull ETF) took in more than $3.8bn last week, the largest weekly inflow on record and the third straight week of inflows, while the semis index is down 69% from its June peak.

Japan: investors sold $16bn of foreign bonds in September, and Jan-Sep 2026 net sales were the largest since 2005. Large banks and insurers bought a net $34bn, and higher domestic yields make repatriation more attractive.

Gavin Baker (quoted) argues OpenAI's contractual compute commitments are now well below spot compute prices, so hyperscaler revenue growth should accelerate as contracts roll off and reprice. He suggests external financing as a share of the AI infrastructure buildout may be near its peak.

Q3 earnings: consensus expects S&P 500 y/y EPS growth of 27%, with AI infrastructure spending over 50% of EPS growth and hyperscaler capex growth of 116%. Median S&P stock EPS growth is about 9% in Q3 versus 14% in Q2.

Lo Miller's team recommends buying the broadening (SPXXAI outperformed the S&P 500 by 586bps since Oct 6), favours quality (GSP1QUAL) though RSI above 80 implies scope for a sharp reversal if inflation/rates concerns ease, and recommends long ACA-exposed beneficiaries (GSHLCACA) as a defensive midterms trade.
Stat of the day: AI hyperscaler equities (GSXUHYPR) were 15% lower the last time hyperscaler credit spreads were this wide. AI beneficiaries versus the rest of the market are down 25% from highs.
Calendar: Netflix and SpaceX report Tuesday, Meta and IBM Wednesday, and NVDA hosts GTC Berlin Tuesday to Thursday.
